A_target.statement:
Regard a [[Definition:Group|group]] $G$ as a category $\mathbf B G$ with one object $\ast$ and $\map {\operatorname {Hom} } {\ast, \ast} = G$.
Then [[Definition:Functor|functors]] $\mathbf B G \to \mathbf B H$ are exactly the [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|homomorphisms]] $G \to H$, and natural transformations $\phi \Rightarrow \psi$ are exactly the elements $h \in H$ with $\map \psi g = h \map \phi g h^{-1}$ for all $g$.

B_source.statement: A [[Definition:Metacategory|category]] consists of objects and morphisms with an associative composition and identity morphisms; a functor preserves composition and identities, and a natural transformation is a family of morphisms commuting with the images of all morphisms.

object_map.reformulation: Transport group theory into category theory by viewing a group as a category with one object in which every morphism is invertible.

validity_conditions: The group axioms are exactly the category axioms with one object, plus invertibility of every morphism.
Functors from BG to Set are G-sets, and to vector spaces are linear representations.
proof_plan:
Associativity and the identity of $G$ are the category axioms of $\mathbf B G$, and every morphism is invertible.
Conversely, such a one-object category is a group.
A functor $\mathbf B G \to \mathbf B H$ sends $\ast$ to $\ast$ and satisfies $\map F {g g'} = \map F g \map F {g'}$ and $\map F e = e$, so it is a homomorphism, and conversely.
A natural transformation $\phi \Rightarrow \psi$ has a single component $h \in H$, and the naturality square says $h \map \phi g = \map \psi g h$ for all $g$.

Hence natural transformations between homomorphisms are conjugating elements, and functors $\mathbf B G \to \mathbf {Set}$ are [[Definition:Group Action|$G$-sets]].
{{qed}}
